subject: Film & Cinema
title: Australian New Wave: Outback on Screen
description: A fast breakdown of Australian New Wave: Outback on Screen for builders.

hook.text: In the 1970s, Australia decided its stories deserved its own cinema — not just Hollywood's.

buildup.text: Government funding fueled films like Picnic at Hanging Rock and Mad Max.

discovery.text: Peter Weir and George Miller created globally successful films with distinctly Australian voices.

twist.text: Many of these directors eventually left for Hollywood, draining Australia's talent.

climax.text: The Australian New Wave proved small countries could build world-class film industries.

punchline.text: The outback produced Hollywood's next generation.

quiz.question: What enabled the Australian New Wave?
